_strings.@@e70fbf028f46: Treaty conformity — KY conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from KY income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the KY return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Kentucky's resident return (Form 740) starts from federal adjusted gross income — 2025 Form 740 line 5 is "Enter amount from federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a", i.e. federal AGI, and Kentucky law requires the individual income tax return to begin with federal adjusted gross income and be adjusted for any differences to arrive at Kentucky adjusted gross income (Form 740 line 6 additions from Schedule M line 6, line 8 subtractions from Schedule M line 17, line 9 Kentucky AGI). The 2025 Schedule M "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" (Part I, lines 1-5, totaled on line 6) are: (1) interest on other states' obligations / taxable mutual-fund dividends, (2) resident adjustment from Kentucky Schedule K-1, (3) special depreciation/Section 179 differences, (4) federal net operating loss, and (5) "other additions" (reservist/National Guard expenses, the lump-sum distribution capital-gains portion, passive activity loss adjustment, pension/IRA basis differences, intangible-asset and depreciable-property gain differences, Armed Forces moving expenses, Kentucky excess business loss limitation). NONE of these add back federally tax-treaty-exempt income. Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and KY has no add-back for it, it is not re-taxed by Kentucky — therefore KY conforms. (Kentucky's starting basis is the Internal Revenue Code in effect as of December 31, 2024, per the live KY DOR Individual Income Tax page.)
_strings.@@e8c189982279: Family Size Tax Credit — Resident individuals/families with modified gross income (MGI) at or below the Schedule ITC Section C table ceiling for their family size. Family size is capped at 4 (yourself, spouse if living in the same household, and qualifying children). Available even to someone claimed as a dependent on a parent's return (family size 1). The 2025 Form 740 line 5 prints the outer gate directly — "If total of Columns A and B is $42,760 or less, you may qualify for the Family Size Tax Credit."

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: Form 740 Line 12 = Line 11 (Taxable Income = Line 9 Kentucky AGI minus Line 10 deduction) x 4% (.04) — printed on the 2025 form: "Tax Computation: Multiply line 11 by 4% (.04) or amount from Schedule J". Line 5 starts from federal AGI (federal Form 1040/1040-SR line 11a); Line 6 adds Schedule M line 6 additions and Line 8 subtracts Schedule M line 17 subtractions. This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Standard deduction change: $3,270 for 2025, up from $3,160 (2024) and $2,980 (2023). The rate is UNCHANGED at 4% (.04) — verified twice (2025 Form 740 line 12 and the live KY DOR Individual Income Tax page). Never carry a Kentucky rate or standard deduction to another tax year without re-verifying that year's own Form 740. Kentucky allows ONE $3,270 standard deduction per return — a joint return gets a single $3,270 (it is NOT doubled); spouses filing separately on a combined return (Filing Status 2) enter $3,270 in each of Columns A and B, which is why the form says "in Columns A and/or B". Kentucky has NO head-of-household filing status. The 2025 Form 740 prints only four statuses: 1 Single, 2 Married filing separately on this combined return, 3 Married filing joint return, 4 Married filing separate returns. The head_of_household column exists only because the engine's schema requires all four federal statuses; it carries the same single $3,270 — a filer who is head of household federally files Kentucky as Single (or married, as applicable). Kentucky has no personal or dependent exemptions; the nonrefundable personal tax credits ($40 age 65+, $40 blind, $20 Kentucky National Guard as of 12/31/2025 — 2025 Schedule ITC Section B, Form 740 line 17), the Family Size Tax Credit (Form 740 lines 20-21, from the Schedule ITC Section C Tax Year 2025 table; the form's line 5 gate is federal AGI of $42,760 or less), the Education Tuition Tax Credit (line 23, Form 8863-K) and the 20% Child and Dependent Care Credit (line 24) are all CREDITS against tax and are NOT modeled by calc.state_tax. Not modeled: Schedule J (farm income averaging) as an alternative to the line 12 multiplication, the line 13 add-ons (Form 4972-K lump-sum tax, Schedule RC-R / DS-R recapture, Angel Investor recapture), the line 27 Kentucky Use Tax, and Kentucky LOCAL occupational license taxes (county/city payroll taxes).
